profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21721 Filigree Court, Suite B, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC11 data center at 21721 Filigree Court, Suite B, in Ashburn, Virginia, sharing its street address with Equinix's DC6 building tracked elsewhere in this registry at Suite A on the same Filigree Court campus cluster. Equinix's own DC11 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 116,831 square feet of space, the largest published footprint among the Ashburn DC-numbered buildings on this campus, a two story reinforced concrete structure, N+1 power redundancy on both UPS and generator systems, generator autonomy rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, and ten compliance certifications including LEED alongside HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. Equinix's own page also cites free cooling and grey water reuse as sustainability features specific to DC11, a distinguishing fact not listed on the DC1, DC3, or DC5 pages nearby on this same campus. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC11 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and Equinix markets DC10 through DC12 alongside DC1 through DC6 collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the East Coast, without singling out DC11's own peering density or customer roster.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
Equinix DC11 is a 116,831 square foot, two-story building in Ashburn with N+1 redundancy on both power and cooling systems, a 30-hour minimum generator runtime at full load, and ten certifications spanning HIPAA, FISMA High, SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27001. The facility publishes no megawatt power capacity, so its IT load cannot be estimated from operator disclosures alone. It distinguishes itself within the nearby DC1, DC3, and DC5 buildings on the same campus by listing free cooling and grey water reuse as sustainability features neither of those buildings claim.

DC11 sits within Equinix's 15-building Washington D.C. metro cluster, which Equinix markets collectively as serving one of the top three internet peering exchanges on the US East Coast. Equinix does not publish a combined power or footprint total for this group, and Loudoun County as a whole operates roughly 10 million square feet of data center space across all operators, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of power region-wide. Among Virginia's mapped facilities, Equinix's published campuses rank 26th by announced megawatt capacity, though this specific reading cannot place DC11 individually within that ranking because Equinix does not disclose its power draw.

Virginia's new GS-5 rate class for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, requires large demand customers like Equinix to sign 14-year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, creating a regulatory binding constraint on expansions in the state. No further power pricing or grid interconnection details for this facility are published.
